screenshots.name: 1-progress
screenshots.caption: Each k3s node shows its setup steps at http://<host name>.local:8080 while it sets up.

screenshots.name: 01-instances
screenshots.caption: The Instances page lists every Cupcake instance with its state, address, images and owner.

screenshots.name: 02-new-instance
screenshots.caption: New instance: choose the slug, which names the instance's address, and optionally the image tag.

screenshots.name: 03-domains
screenshots.caption: Domains lists the host names cupcake-master answers on and how each is reached.

screenshots.name: 04-remote-access
screenshots.caption: Remote access sets up a Cloudflare tunnel or the Tailscale operator for reaching the cluster from outside.

screenshots.name: 05-trust
screenshots.caption: Trust explains how to make devices trust this cluster's own certificate authority.

screenshots.name: 06-models
screenshots.caption: Models lists the transcription models kept for every instance, and which is the default.

screenshots.name: 07-users
screenshots.caption: Users lists the accounts, their state and instance limit, and the sign-up settings.

screenshots.name: 08-logs
screenshots.caption: Logs shows the recent output of cupcake-master's own components.

screenshots.name: 09-notifications
screenshots.caption: Notifications lists everything cupcake-master has told you, newest first.

screenshots.name: 10-notification-menu
screenshots.caption: The bell opens the latest notifications; unread ones are marked.

screenshots.name: 11-account-menu
screenshots.caption: The account menu chooses the light, dark or automatic appearance and signs out.

screenshots.name: 12-tooltip
screenshots.caption: Icon buttons name their action when the pointer rests on them.

screenshots.name: 13-backups
screenshots.caption: Backups sets where every night's backups are copied off the node, and lists the backups kept on it.

screenshots.name: 01-instances
screenshots.caption: The Instances page lists every Cupcake instance with its state, address, images and owner. In the dark theme, which follows the computer's setting by default.

screenshots.name: 03-domains
screenshots.caption: Domains lists the host names cupcake-master answers on and how each is reached. In the dark theme, which follows the computer's setting by default.

screenshots.name: 04-remote-access
screenshots.caption: Remote access sets up a Cloudflare tunnel or the Tailscale operator for reaching the cluster from outside. In the dark theme, which follows the computer's setting by default.

screenshots.name: 07-users
screenshots.caption: Users lists the accounts, their state and instance limit, and the sign-up settings. In the dark theme, which follows the computer's setting by default.

screenshots.name: 1-api-access
screenshots.caption: API access on an instance's page lists the tokens that let scripts manage it.

screenshots.name: 2-filled
screenshots.caption: Name the token, choose what it may do and when it expires, then choose Create token.

screenshots.name: 3-shown-once
screenshots.caption: Copy the token straight away; it is shown only once.

screenshots.name: 4-replaced
screenshots.caption: Replace the token gives a new one, shown once; the old one stops working at once.

screenshots.name: 5-revoked
screenshots.caption: Revoke removes the token.

screenshots.name: 1-instance
screenshots.caption: Back up now is among the actions at the top of an instance's page.

screenshots.name: 2-queued
screenshots.caption: The backup is queued and shown in the task history.

screenshots.name: 3-listed
screenshots.caption: When it finishes, the backup is listed under Backups, where it can be restored or deleted.

screenshots.name: 1-domains
screenshots.caption: Domains, in the top menu, lists the host names cupcake-master itself answers on.

screenshots.name: 2-filled
screenshots.caption: Enter the host name, choose HTTPS, self-signed certificate when you have no certificate for it yet, then choose Add domain.

screenshots.name: 3-self-signed
screenshots.caption: The domain is served over HTTPS with a self-signed certificate; browsers warn about it until a signed certificate is uploaded.

screenshots.name: 4-upload
screenshots.caption: Use a signed certificate asks for the certificate, with any intermediates, and its key.

screenshots.name: 5-own-certificate
screenshots.caption: The domain now uses your certificate; its expiry is shown, and staff are warned two weeks before it.

screenshots.name: 6-removed
screenshots.caption: Remove takes the domain and its certificate away.

screenshots.name: 1-warning
screenshots.caption: Delete instance, at the bottom of an instance's page, says what is removed and when; only staff see it.

screenshots.name: 2-confirm
screenshots.caption: Type the instance's slug to confirm; Delete instance is only available once it matches.

screenshots.name: 3-scheduled
screenshots.caption: The instance is stopped at once and kept until the date shown; its owner is told.

screenshots.name: 4-listed
screenshots.caption: On the Instances page it is marked with the day it will be deleted.

screenshots.name: 5-recovered
screenshots.caption: Recover, before that date, cancels the deletion and starts the instance again.

screenshots.name: 6-delete-now
screenshots.caption: To delete it without waiting, type its slug again under the date and choose Delete now.

screenshots.name: 7-deleted
screenshots.caption: Once deleted, its programs, database and files are gone; the page keeps its history.

screenshots.name: 1-domains
screenshots.caption: Domains on an instance's page lists every host name the instance answers on.

screenshots.name: 2-filled
screenshots.caption: Enter another host name, such as ct-b9c044-docs.local, and how it is reached, then choose Add domain. Under the cluster's domain an instance may use its slug followed by -<name>.

screenshots.name: 3-added
screenshots.caption: The domain is added and the instance is updated to answer on it.

screenshots.name: 4-removed
screenshots.caption: Remove takes the domain away again; the main domain cannot be removed.

screenshots.name: 1-form
screenshots.caption: Choose New instance on the Instances page.

screenshots.name: 2-filled
screenshots.caption: Enter a slug of 4 to 32 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens; it names the instance's address. Leave the image tag empty for the current release.

screenshots.name: 3-queued
screenshots.caption: The new instance's page opens; its provisioning is queued.

screenshots.name: 4-provisioning
screenshots.caption: While it is provisioned, the task history shows the running task.

screenshots.name: 5-active
screenshots.caption: Once active, the instance answers at its address, shown under Domains.

screenshots.name: 0-wrong-password
screenshots.caption: A wrong email address or password is refused with a message.

screenshots.name: 1-sign-in-form
screenshots.caption: The sign-in page of cupcake-master.

screenshots.name: 2-sign-in-filled
screenshots.caption: Enter the email address and password of your account, then choose Sign in.

screenshots.name: 3-signed-in
screenshots.caption: After signing in, cupcake-master opens on the Instances page.

screenshots.name: 1-suspending
screenshots.caption: Suspend stops the instance's programs but keeps its data; confirm when asked.

screenshots.name: 2-suspended
screenshots.caption: A suspended instance shows Resume instead of Suspend.

screenshots.name: 3-resumed
screenshots.caption: Resume starts it again; it is active once its programs answer.
